editorial.headline: Conventional Financial-Institution Pension Funds: Open Nationally, Viable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity manages conventional defined-contribution pension programmes for individuals, from employees to independent workers, with a clear national opening for foreign investment.
editorial.body:
This activity is the conventional management of pension funds established by financial institutions. Its practical focus is a defined-contribution pension programme for individuals: employees as well as independent workers. The programme sits separately from the employer pension fund maintained for employees of the relevant bank or life-insurance company. That separation is central to the activity’s character. It is not simply a general savings arrangement, but the administration of an individual pension programme within the conventional financial-institution pension-fund model.

The code is open to businesses at every stated scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth matters because the record does not confine the activity to one end of the business spectrum. The same defined-contribution pension-fund activity is therefore presented as available across those four scales, while retaining the specific institutional setting described in its scope: conventional pension-fund management by a financial institution, for individual participants whose arrangement is separate from the employer fund of the associated bank or life-insurance company.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is unambiguous. The activity is open to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, the record places no foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity nationally. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. That national position should be read for what it says: a conventional financial-institution pension-fund activity may be foreign-owned up to the stated ceiling, rather than being described as nationally reserved or restricted by a lower percentage in this record.

Bali does not reverse that conclusion. The province’s standing is **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the activity is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium. The reason is risk classification at the Large scale: it is Medium-High/High risk, rather than within the Low or Medium-Low risk categories covered by the island-wide permanent PMA moratorium. The relevant Bali rule blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities; this activity falls outside that block on the record provided. For a foreign-owned registration in Bali, the honest reading is therefore neither a special Bali ownership cap nor a moratorium prohibition, but an activity recorded as not blocked because its Large-scale OSS risk position is Medium-High/High.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not reverse the national opening: this activity is recorded as outside the province’s PMA moratorium block.
